packs.title: Metal, Stone and Sky
packs.promise: Find a wider Madrid in metal spirals, a stone voyage and the shapes between northern towers.

q.s: Collect three different ways a bridge holds a space open.
st: Choose three visible boundaries in the bridge or its official image: a metal spiral, a patch of mesh and a solid deck or edge.
Give each boundary a short job name based on what it appears to separate, hold or let through. These are your descriptions of visible form, not engineering claims.
Make a three-item collection with each job name and its boundary. Choose which leaves the most air visible from your viewpoint; no measurement or movement is required.

q.s: Collect a frame, a clear panel and a planted shape in a glasshouse.
st: In the official glasshouse image or a comfortable exterior view, find a structural frame, a glazed panel and a planted shape visible behind or beside it.
Describe what each part contributes to the idea of a sheltered garden: a boundary, a view or something growing. Do not infer a plant’s species, temperature or needs from its appearance.
Save the three parts and their contributions. Give this small collection your own two-word name; leave the real glasshouse and plants as they are.

q.s: Turn an ornate entrance into a design for an imaginary stage curtain.
st: Choose one curling detail and one heavier edge in the main entrance, using the official frontage photograph if the view is obscured.
Invent a stage curtain with one broad fold inspired by the curling detail and a border inspired by the heavier edge. Draw it, or describe the fold and border in words.
Give your curtain an original title and save the two architectural starting points with your design. It is an imagined curtain, not an announced performance or a design by the centre.

packs.title: Patterns in the Open
packs.promise: Find a Madrid story in the shapes between squares and gardens.

q.s: Collect a rhythm above the garden.
st: Choose a comfortable public path in Plaza de Oriente with a view of the Royal Palace. Stay outside planted beds and any controlled palace area.
Find three repeated shapes on the façade: a window shape, a vertical divider and a detail near the roofline. Count a small group of each; you do not need to count the whole building.
Choose the repeat that feels quickest and the one that feels slowest. Explain your choice through spacing or size.
Save your three shapes and your fast-and-slow comparison.

q.s: Collect what the pond repeats and what it changes.
st: Check the park’s current signs, then choose a comfortable west-side path viewpoint of Estanque Grande, well back from the water.
Find one solid outline above the pond and its reflection. Compare where the reflected outline holds together and where it breaks into smaller pieces.
Collect a second reflected shape or colour, then find something that the water does not copy clearly.
Save your two reflections and the detail that resisted becoming a clear copy.

q.s: Turn a living outline into an imaginary route.
st: Choose a comfortable place on an open public path, with a leaf or small branch shape visible from where you stop. Leave it growing where it is.
Follow its outline or branching lines with your eyes. Imagine those lines as a tiny map.
Draw or describe three stops on that imagined route and give each an original place name based on its shape, such as a bend or a pointed end.
Add one sentence explaining how a traveller would get from the first stop to the last. Save your map.
